about: The audit of the source article (source/article.json), by Karan Deshmukh. Each finding quotes the source, says why it matters, and says what the migrated documentation does instead. Accuracy findings were checked against the Keycloak 26.8.2 server's recorded behaviour in content/projects/keycloak/evidence.json.

findings.quote: Simply delete the OTP and the user will be asked to setup 2FA again on their next login.
findings.problem: False in Keycloak 26.8.2. With the default browser flow, a user whose OTP credential was deleted signs in with the password alone, and nothing asks them to set up a new authenticator. The account is left with one factor.
findings.fix: The how-to adds the step that was missing: Configure OTP in Required user actions, then Save. A caution says why the step matters.

findings.quote: Sometimes users lose their phone and can't login anymore.
findings.problem: Nothing asks the administrator to confirm that the request comes from the account's owner. A reset on a request from someone else hands them the account.
findings.fix: A shared Before you start section, reused by the how-to and the troubleshooting page, asks for confirmation through contact details given before the phone was lost.

findings.problem: Three names for one thing, none of them defined. Keycloak's console calls it OTP: the credential type is Otp and the required action is Configure OTP. A translator, a search engine and a reader each see three subjects.
findings.fix: One term, one-time password (OTP), defined once on the concept page and recorded in the terminology list for translation.

findings.quote: go to users … click on credentials tab
findings.problem: The labels don't match the interface (Users, Credentials), and the steps skip the realm: an administrator of the master realm searches the wrong realm's users.
findings.fix: Interface labels in bold, exactly as the console shows them, and a first step that checks the current realm.

findings.problem: Bold text in place of a heading, and step numbers typed into paragraphs. Screen readers and the help center's own table of contents see no structure, and one task is mixed with background and settings.
findings.fix: Real headings and an ordered list, and the content split by purpose: a concept, a how-to, a reference and a troubleshooting page.

findings.problem: The reader can't tell success from failure, and nothing records what was done.
findings.fix: A Check that it worked section: the new Otp row, its date, and the admin events Keycloak keeps.

findings.quote: If it still doesn't work please contact IT.
findings.problem: No symptom, no cause, no action, and the reader is often IT.
findings.fix: A troubleshooting page organised by what the user sees, each with its cause and the fix, reproduced on the server.

findings.problem: No alternative text and no caption. A reader who can't see the picture loses its content, and nobody can tell which step it belongs to.
findings.fix: Each screenshot has alternative text that says what is marked, sits under the step it shows, and has its sensitive values hidden.

findings.quote: You can change the MFA settings here
findings.problem: "here" says nothing out of context, and screen-reader users often move from link to link.
findings.fix: Link text that names the destination: Keycloak OTP policy.

findings.quote: a piece of cake … secs … Last updated 3/4/25
findings.problem: An idiom that doesn't translate, an abbreviation, an exclamation, and a date that means 3 April in France and 4 March in the US.
findings.fix: Plain wording, units in full, and dates kept by the publishing system in ISO 8601, so each locale can show its own format.

findings.quote: can't login … Login to Keycloak … setup 2FA
findings.problem: Login and setup are nouns. The verbs are sign in and set up.
findings.fix: Sign in and set up as verbs, everywhere, enforced by a Vale substitution rule.

findings.problem: No owner, no reviewer, no review date, no product version and no audience. Nobody knows when the article stops being true, and it says nothing about the Keycloak version it describes.
findings.fix: Front matter on every page: owner, audience, product version, last review and review interval. The Git history records every change and who approved it.

findings.problem: It opens with the user's problem, but every step is an administrator's. A user who finds it can do none of it.
findings.fix: The how-to says who it's for in its first lines. The user's side, setting up the new phone, is one step with its own screenshot.

findings.problem: Simply tells a reader who is stuck that the task is easy. Here it also hides the step that makes the reset safe.
findings.fix: No minimisers; Vale flags simply, just and easily.

architecture.title: One-time passwords in Keycloak
architecture.holds: What an OTP credential is, what a required action does, and why deleting a credential doesn't by itself ask for a new one.

architecture.title: Reset a user's OTP credential
architecture.holds: The administrator's task, step by step, with screenshots and the check.

architecture.title: OTP policy settings
architecture.holds: Every setting of the realm's OTP policy, its default in 26.8.2, and the matching REST field.

architecture.title: When a user can't sign in with a one-time password
architecture.holds: Three symptoms, each with its cause and the fix.
